notes:
**Windows** — run `ruze_0.0.32_x64-setup.exe`.
**Linux** — `flatpak install ruze-0.0.32.flatpak`, then `flatpak run com.ruze.chat`.
**Android** — sideload `ruze-0.0.32.apk`. arm64 devices, Android 8.0 or newer.

---

### Added

- **Three ways to start a call with a friend.** Beside their name there is a
  handset, a camera and a screen. All three open the same call and all three
  carry your voice; what they decide is what you arrive with — so sharing a
  screen with somebody is one press rather than starting a call, then finding
  the share button, then picking a screen.

  Nothing is fixed by the choice. A call started as audio becomes a video call
  the moment you turn the camera on, and the person you are talking to sees it
  whenever you do.

### Changed

- **Every icon button says what it does, on hover and on focus.** The call
  controls and the buttons in a conversation now show a label when you point
  at one — and, unlike the tooltip a browser draws by itself, when you tab to
  one. Keyboard users could not see those labels at all before, which is the
  half of "accessible" that having a name does not cover.

- **Ruze asks before taking you out of a call you are in.** You can only be in
  one at a time — one microphone cannot be in two rooms — so starting a new
  call, or answering one, has always left whichever you were in. It just did it
  silently: you pressed a button and were removed from a conversation you were
  having, with nothing said and no way to decline.

  Both now name the call you would be leaving and offer to stay in it.
  Answering is the one that needed it most: a button is pressed deliberately,
  while a ring arrives at a moment you did not choose.
